scope: Corollary 6.3 (Charge versus neutral gap at fixed flux) of the manuscript “A Fock-space inequality and the Laughlin spectral gap” (preprints/A-Fock-space-inequality-and-the-Laughlin-spectral-gap-September-24-2026/A-Fock-space-inequality-and-the-Laughlin-spectral-gap-September-24-2026.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 269 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 46a8f75298d33906), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 15. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: For N ≥ 2, fix QN = 3(N − 1) and write E0(n; QN ) = min spec Hn,QN for the coefficient-one interaction (1). Let GapN be the first positive eigenvalue of HN,QN , its neutral gap. The particle-number charge gap at this same flux, ∆N = E0(N + 1; QN ) + E0(N − 1; QN ) − 2E0(N; QN ), satisfies ∆N = E0(N + 1; QN ) ≥ N N − 1 GapN > 0. In particular, ∆N ≥ N/[25(N − 1)] for N ≥ N0, with N0 as in Corollary 1.2.
